last_digest.rss_summary: The developers of Goddess of Victory: NIKKE have confirmed that hackers tampered with the game's PC launcher scripts in a supply-chain attack, distributing malware capable of stealing credentials and cryptocurrency wallet data. [...]

last_digest.title: DreamHost confirms data breach exposed FTP logins and webmail sessions
last_digest.rss_summary: DreamHost is warning of a data breach after attackers gained access to its File Manager platform for two months and stole customers' FTP/SFTP usernames and passwords. [...]

last_digest.title: More Asian airlines announce data breaches after attack on Spanish IT provider Amadeus
last_digest.rss_summary: Japan Airlines, Cathay Pacific, Korean Air, Asiana Airlines, Singapore Airlines and Malaysia Airlines have all come forward over the last week to report data breaches traced back to Amadeus IT Group — a company that builds and maintains platforms for flight reservation, ticketing and check-in platforms.

last_digest.title: Rigged Coding Assignment, Abused AI Tool Opened Path to $6 Billion Binance Heist
last_digest.rss_summary:
Binance’s first incident report traces the record theft to a months-long campaign that compromised three engineers’ computers.
The post Rigged Coding Assignment, Abused AI Tool Opened Path to $6 Billion Binance Heist appeared first on SecurityWeek.

last_week_digest.title: Magento Campaign Infects 953 Online Stores Across Five Domains
last_week_digest.tldr: A sophisticated skimming campaign has compromised 953 Magento online stores since July 2025, using advanced bot-filtering techniques to evade security scanners. This persistent threat highlights significant vulnerabilities in e-commerce content management systems, signalling an urgent need for robust integrity monitoring to protect global consumer data.

last_week_digest.title: Gheist Attackers Stumble in Attempt to Abuse GitHub Tokens
last_week_digest.tldr: The Gheist campaign compromised 850 accounts, injecting malicious workflows across 13,500 GitHub branches to harvest sensitive credentials. While platform controls mitigated public repository risks, private enterprise environments remain exposed, signalling that stolen tokens continue to weaponise legitimate automation features against global supply chains.

last_week_digest.title: Ukraine warns hackers are exploiting Chinese-made Dahua surveillance cameras
last_week_digest.tldr: Ukrainian cybersecurity authorities warn that hackers are exploiting vulnerabilities in Dahua surveillance cameras to compromise over 14,500 devices. This breach, enabling remote access to sensitive video feeds, highlights critical supply chain risks and signals an urgent need for global organisations to prioritise firmware security.

last_week_digest.title: Energy giant ENGIE discloses data breach affecting customers
last_week_digest.tldr: French energy giant ENGIE confirmed a data breach involving a third-party marketing platform, exposing contact details and contract information for French customers. This incident highlights the critical operational risk posed by partner-managed tools, signalling that supply chain vulnerabilities remain a primary target for global enterprises.

last_week_digest.title: Stolen AI Reasoning Could Help China Build Cheaper Rivals
last_week_digest.tldr: Chinese entities have systematically extracted billions of tokens from Western frontier AI models to train rival systems through distillation. This exploitation of API reasoning traces threatens intellectual property, signalling that securing proprietary model architectures is now a critical operational priority for global technology firms.

last_week_digest.title: Japan's GMO urges customers to shut down PCs amid ransomware threat
last_week_digest.tldr: Japan’s GMO Internet Group faces a severe crisis after hackers breached its Onamae Desktop Cloud, potentially compromising 26,739 servers. The firm refused a $50 million ransom demand, leading to data leaks and urgent customer shutdowns. This incident highlights the critical vulnerability of cloud infrastructure to credential-based attacks and extortion threats.

last_week_digest.title: Three Japan-Focused Cyberattacks Show How Hackers Use AI
last_week_digest.tldr: Three cyberattacks targeting nineteen organisations in Japan demonstrate how hackers leverage AI to automate reconnaissance and exploit legacy systems. These incidents, including one using forty-four AI agents, signal a shift toward scalable, low-traffic attacks. This evolution forces global businesses to prioritise securing public-facing infrastructure against increasingly efficient, AI-driven threat actor operations.

last_week_digest.title: External Teams Chats Anchor 15-Minute Malware Delivery
last_week_digest.tldr: Black Basta affiliates are exploiting Microsoft Teams’ external chat functionality to deliver malware within fifteen minutes of initial contact. This social engineering campaign targets global organisations, bypassing traditional security perimeters to facilitate ransomware deployment. The attack signals a critical shift toward abusing trusted enterprise collaboration tools to accelerate operational disruption.

last_week_digest.title: Nefilim, Hive ransomware operator given five-year-plus sentence after guilty plea
last_week_digest.tldr: Artem Stryzhak, a prolific ransomware affiliate, received a 70-month prison sentence for attacks against hospitals and government entities across 80 countries. His activities, involving both Nefilim and Hive groups, caused over $100 million in losses. This prosecution signals a growing global commitment to dismantling ransomware syndicates through multi-continent legal cooperation.

last_week_digest.title: Secrets Management Firm Infisical Valued at $600 Million After $40 Million Raise
last_week_digest.tldr: Secrets management firm Infisical has secured $40 million in Series B funding, reaching a $600 million valuation. Serving 1,300 organisations including Airbus and Volkswagen, the company aims to mitigate risks posed by AI agents. This investment signals that securing machine-to-machine credentials is now a critical priority for global enterprise cybersecurity strategies.

last_week_digest.title: GhostAction Hacking Wave Fizzles, But Attackers Lurk on in GitHub
last_week_digest.tldr: The GhostAction campaign targeting developer endpoints and cloud infrastructure highlights a growing shift toward supply chain exploitation. By infiltrating GitHub repositories, attackers threaten global software integrity, forcing organisations to rethink security protocols as these persistent threats signal a broader, dangerous evolution in cybercrime tactics.

last_week_digest.title: 345,000 email addresses stolen in cyberattack on Germany’s far-right party AfD
last_week_digest.tldr: A cyberattack on Germany’s AfD party exposed 345,000 email addresses, compromising internal communications and sensitive voter data. This breach highlights significant vulnerabilities in political IT infrastructure, signalling that organisations must urgently prioritise robust security protocols to protect against politically motivated data exfiltration and reputational damage.

last_week_digest.title: Volt Typhoon hides zero-day attacks using 'Silent Train' framework
last_week_digest.tldr: The state-sponsored group Volt Typhoon is utilising the Silent Train framework to launch stealthy zero-day attacks against critical global infrastructure. By rotating compromised relay devices, the actors maintain persistent access, signalling a shift toward highly evasive, targeted operations that threaten operational continuity for international enterprises.

last_week_digest.title: Japan Airlines warns of data breach as country grapples with multiple cyber incidents
last_week_digest.tldr: Japan Airlines confirmed a data breach at IT provider Amadeus, exposing personal records of 92,000 customers. This incident, alongside millions of records stolen from other Japanese firms, signals a systemic vulnerability in third-party supply chains, prompting urgent government intervention to bolster national cybersecurity resilience.

last_week_digest.title: China-Linked Hackers Exploit PHP2Shell to Root Firewalls
last_week_digest.tldr: China-linked hackers exploited critical PHP vulnerabilities to compromise 24 firewalls, eventually infiltrating a government-affiliated management server to harvest credentials and domain data. This targeted operation highlights a growing trend of nation-state actors weaponising edge device flaws to gain persistent, high-level access to internal networks.

last_week_digest.title: Chinese hackers used VMware ESX zero-day; PHP2Shell and Fragnesia chained to root firewalls
last_week_digest.tldr: China-nexus threat actors are exploiting VMware ESX zero-days and chaining Linux kernel vulnerabilities to compromise critical infrastructure globally. By rooting 25 firewalls across Asia and North America, attackers gained persistent access to sensitive networks. This sophisticated campaign signals a shift toward weaponising edge devices, forcing organisations to prioritise rapid patching and enhanced audit visibility.

last_week_digest.title: Binance hit by $6.3 billion theft in what could be the biggest crypto heist on record
last_week_digest.tldr: Binance suffered a historic $6.3 billion cryptocurrency theft after attackers compromised a DevOps engineer’s laptop to manipulate withdrawal systems. While $2.7 billion was frozen by industry partners, the breach highlights critical vulnerabilities in centralised exchange infrastructure. This massive incident signals an urgent need for enhanced endpoint security and robust signing protocols across global digital assets.

last_week_digest.title: Polymarket halts trading after crypto-draining script breach, $2.5M traced
last_week_digest.tldr: Polymarket suspended trading after hackers compromised a third-party monitoring service to distribute malicious JavaScript, resulting in the theft of approximately $2.5 million in user assets. While the platform restored services and promised full reimbursements, this incident highlights the critical supply chain risks inherent in third-party integrations, signalling a growing vulnerability for global digital exchanges.

last_week_digest.title: $6 Billion Binance Hack Bears Hallmarks of North Korea’s TraderTraitor
last_week_digest.tldr: North Korean state-sponsored hackers siphoned $6.36 billion from Binance in the largest cryptocurrency heist recorded, forcing the exchange to halt withdrawals and pledge full user reimbursements. This sophisticated breach, likely originating from a compromised engineer’s laptop, signals a critical escalation in state-backed cyber threats, highlighting severe vulnerabilities in global digital asset infrastructure security.

last_week_digest.title: Limited reports of PHP bug exploitation emerge
last_week_digest.tldr: Chinese threat actors recently exploited two PHP vulnerabilities, dubbed PHP2Shell, to compromise 24 firewalls, including government-affiliated servers. By chaining these bugs with secondary exploits, attackers gained root access to extract credentials. This campaign signals a shift toward highly targeted, bespoke exploitation tactics, forcing global organisations to accelerate patching cycles against increasingly sophisticated, automated reconnaissance.

last_week_digest.title: Ransomware gang talked AI agents into doing much of its dirty work
last_week_digest.tldr: The GOLD OGRE ransomware group is leveraging AI agents to automate network reconnaissance and credential theft, successfully compromising three victims identified on their data leak site. By masking malicious prompts as authorised red team activities, attackers bypassed safety guardrails. This shift signals a dangerous industry trend where AI accelerates attack chains, reducing required technical expertise.

last_week_digest.title: Florida warns that 4.9 million people had Social Security numbers leaked in financial aid site breach
last_week_digest.tldr: The Florida Department of Education confirmed a significant data breach exposing the Social Security numbers and personal details of 4.9 million financial aid applicants. This incident, causing temporary service disruptions, highlights a growing trend of state-level educational systems becoming primary targets for cybercriminals, signalling an urgent need for enhanced public sector data protection strategies.

last_week_digest.title: Yoba Malware Hides a Crypto Miner Behind Legitimate OpenAI and Anthropic Binaries
last_week_digest.tldr: The Yoba malware campaign exploits SEO poisoning and fake GitHub projects to distribute cryptocurrency miners disguised as legitimate OpenAI and Anthropic tools. By leveraging DLL sideloading and signed binaries, attackers bypass security protections on infected systems. This trend signals a growing risk where threat actors weaponise popular AI software to compromise enterprise environments globally.

last_week_digest.title: FBI Flags Over 600 Addresses Tied to North Korea’s Binance Heist
last_week_digest.tldr: North Korean state-sponsored hackers stole $6.3 billion from Binance in the largest cryptocurrency heist recorded. The breach, involving sophisticated automation and multiple entry points, forced Binance to cover massive losses using corporate funds. This event signals a critical escalation in cyber-espionage capabilities, highlighting the severe systemic risks facing global digital asset platforms today.

last_week_digest.title: Chainalysis Investigates Security Incident Involving AI-Driven Attack Techniques
last_week_digest.tldr: Chainalysis recently suffered a security breach where attackers utilised offensive AI agents to access sensitive user data, including full names, email addresses, and organisation roles. While core investigation tools remained secure, the incident signals a concerning industry shift towards automated, AI-driven threats, forcing firms to rapidly enhance system hardening and defensive security protocols.

last_week_digest.title: Michigan State cyber incident claimed by ransomware gang behind recent hospital attack
last_week_digest.tldr: The BYOD ransomware gang claimed a breach of Michigan State University, allegedly compromising personal data belonging to 1.3 million individuals. This incident, following attacks on medical facilities, highlights an escalating trend of threat actors targeting large educational institutions, forcing widespread operational disruption and credential resets.

last_week_digest.title: Stolen AI access leaves companies with cloud bills of up to $1 million
last_week_digest.tldr: Cybercriminals are hijacking corporate cloud accounts to run AI models, leaving victims with bills reaching $1 million. This LLMJacking trend, affecting global financial and technology sectors, signals a shift toward monetising stolen API keys, forcing organisations to urgently secure backend infrastructure against rapid, high-cost exploitation.

last_week_digest.title: New wave of fridge cyberattacks hits European supermarkets, this time in Belgium, Luxembourg, Sweden and Estonia
last_week_digest.tldr: Cyberattacks targeting refrigeration systems across Belgium, Luxembourg, Sweden, and Estonia have caused widespread food spoilage and fire risks in dozens of supermarkets. By remotely triggering defrost modes, attackers exposed critical vulnerabilities in industrial IoT infrastructure, signalling an urgent need for enhanced supply chain security.

last_week_digest.title: One Compromised Laptop, Billions Lost: The Binance Attack-Path Warning
last_week_digest.tldr: A single compromised laptop recently triggered a catastrophic security failure at Binance, resulting in billions of dollars in losses. This incident highlights how inadequate internal controls and poor system segmentation create systemic risks, signalling that global financial institutions must urgently prioritise robust, multi-layered defence strategies.

last_week_digest.title: Over 100 European Stores Hit as Supermarket Fridge Attacks Return
last_week_digest.tldr: Cyberattacks targeting refrigeration controllers across Europe have impacted over 100 stores, causing significant food spoilage and operational disruption. These incidents, exploiting legacy hardware with exposed interfaces, signal a critical vulnerability in industrial supply chains, highlighting the urgent need for securing internet-connected infrastructure against remote exploitation.

last_week_digest.title: NIKKE PC game launcher hacked to spread remote access, data-stealing malware
last_week_digest.tldr: Hackers compromised the NIKKE game launcher, distributing malware to millions of users to steal credentials and cryptocurrency. This supply-chain attack highlights critical vulnerabilities in content delivery networks, signalling that software providers must urgently enhance integrity monitoring to prevent malicious code injection within legitimate update pipelines.

last_week_digest.title: Russian hackers target iOS and Android users with n-day exploits
last_week_digest.tldr: Russian state-linked hackers, APT29, are deploying n-day exploits against iOS and Android users via compromised websites and supply-chain attacks. This campaign, targeting military and diplomatic sectors, signals a shift toward exploiting unpatched mobile vulnerabilities, threatening data integrity for high-value organisations on a global scale.

last_week_digest.title: DreamHost confirms data breach exposed FTP logins and webmail sessions
last_week_digest.tldr: DreamHost confirmed a two-month security breach exposing FTP and webmail credentials after attackers exploited a File Manager vulnerability between August and October 2026. This incident highlights persistent risks in hosting infrastructure, forcing urgent password resets and signalling a critical need for enhanced platform security.

last_week_digest.title: More Asian airlines announce data breaches after attack on Spanish IT provider Amadeus
last_week_digest.tldr: A cyberattack on Spanish IT provider Amadeus exposed sensitive passenger data across multiple Asian airlines, including Japan Airlines and Singapore Airlines. With over 191,000 records compromised, the incident highlights critical supply chain vulnerabilities, signalling that third-party dependencies remain a major operational risk for global aviation.

last_week_digest.title: Rigged Coding Assignment, Abused AI Tool Opened Path to $6 Billion Binance Heist
last_week_digest.tldr: Binance suffered a $6.34 billion theft after North Korean hackers compromised three engineers’ devices using fake job interviews and malicious AI tools. This breach, which forced the freezing of $2.85 billion in assets, highlights the critical vulnerability of internal development environments to sophisticated social engineering.
